knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 4.1.5
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Name one model-fit measure for comparing nested or candidate linear models. State how it informs keeping vs dropping an X.
hints: Use CMP language from today's notes.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Example: adjusted R² / AIC / similar CMP measure — prefer the model whose fit measure improves without unjustified complexity; drop X when measure and theory do not support it.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Skipping the LO hinge or swallowing the next LO.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 4.1.5
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Two nested linear models for claim severity: M1 uses age only; M2 adds sum insured and NCD. (1) Name two fit measures you could use to choose between candidate explanatory sets and what each rewards or penalises. (2) Refuse: 'Keep every term with p<0.05 and selection is done' and 'kitchen-sink regression (include every column) is a selection warrant.'
knowledge_checks.model_answer: (1) e.g. adjusted R² (rewards fit while adjusting for unused complexity vs raw R²); AIC/BIC (likelihood fit with a parameter-count penalty). (2) Refuse: mechanical p-value chopping is not a complete selection warrant; including every column is not selection — use a fit measure (and theory) to justify the explanatory set. GLM structure is a different topic.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Treating p-value chopping or column-soup as a complete selection warrant.
